kurz: How capital can be converted into regular income, what a lifelong annuity costs, how much more a withdrawal plan pays and why a combination of the two usually performs best.

bloecke.md:
In the accumulation phase, the goal can be measured, namely as much capital as possible on the target date. In the payout phase, the money has to last as long as your life, and nobody knows how long that will be. A 65-year-old man in Germany has on average around 18 more years ahead of him, a 65-year-old woman around 21. This average is of little use for your own planning, because half of all cases lie above it. The difference between a retirement of 13 years and one of 33 years is the difference between a comfortable old age and a destitute one.

There are three solutions to this risk: an insurance policy that takes it over, a withdrawal plan that ignores it, and a combination of the two that splits it.

## Private immediate annuity

The private immediate annuity is a pension insurance policy paid for with a single premium and without an accumulation phase. The customer pays in capital once and receives a pension for life from the following month. Its price is reflected in the **annuity conversion factor** (Rentenfaktor), the guaranteed monthly pension per €10,000 of single premium. Only this figure allows two offers to be compared. All other figures in the sales brochure are projections.

Three quantities determine the annuity conversion factor. The first is the **technical interest rate** (Rechnungszins), at which the insurer pays interest on the capital not yet paid out. Since 1 January 2025, the maximum technical interest rate (Höchstrechnungszins) has been 1.0% (Section 2 DeckRV, Actuarial Reserves Ordinance), and it limits what may be guaranteed at all. The second is the **mortality table**. The calculation uses the annuity mortality table of the German Association of Actuaries (Deutsche Aktuarvereinigung), which assumes considerably longer lifespans than population statistics. This is partly due to built-in safety margins and partly because it is mainly people who feel healthy who convert their capital into an annuity. The third quantity is costs. Acquisition costs may be offset in the actuarial reserve (Deckungsrückstellung) at no more than 2.5% of the total premiums (maximum Zillmer rate under Section 4 DeckRV). This rule does not limit the amount of the agreed acquisition costs. Administration costs are also charged on every single pension payment.

bloecke.formel: Monthly pension = single premium ÷ 10,000 × annuity conversion factor
bloecke.erklaerung: The annuity conversion factor combines the technical interest rate, mortality table and costs into a single figure. A guaranteed annuity conversion factor applies regardless of how interest rates and life expectancy develop. A factor that is merely “currently valid” may be lowered by the insurer up to the start of the pension.

bloecke.titel: From a fixed-term annuity to a guaranteed immediate annuity
bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation for €100,000, pension starting at 65, notional payout period of 30 years; the starting point is a simple fixed-term annuity at 2%.

bloecke.md:
In this model, €100,000 becomes around €307 of guaranteed monthly pension, which corresponds to an annuity conversion factor of 30.7. The difference from a fixed-term annuity of your own is the price for two things. One is the guarantee that the pension will be paid until the last insured person has died. The other is the cautious calculation prescribed by supervisory law.

In addition, there is the profit participation (Überschussbeteiligung). If the insurer earns more than the technical interest rate, the pension rises above the guaranteed level. Using as an approximation the current rate of interest of 2.54% that Assekurata determined in March 2026 as the average for new endowment policies (Kapitallebensversicherungen), the same calculation would give around €380. This amount is only projected and not promised, and it can be cut in bad years.

Every offer states a guaranteed pension and a projected pension, and the projected one is usually presented more prominently. Providers can only be compared on the basis of the guaranteed pension. A household budget that relies on the projection contains money to which there is no entitlement.

A second point concerns applicants in poor health. A health assessment that would get them a higher pension is practically unavailable on the German market. People with a reduced life expectancy therefore pay the same price as everyone else and thus subsidise the healthy.

## Withdrawal plan

A withdrawal plan, by contrast, is a fixed-term annuity. Capital and interest are spread over a fixed number of years, after which the account is empty. The result can be calculated to the cent. The capital remains the investor's property, it can be inherited and is available at any time, and there are no costs for an insurance wrapper.

However, the range of offers on the market is small. Withdrawal plans from banks with an interest rate guaranteed for twenty years are hardly available in Germany. You usually have to build such a plan yourself, for example from fixed-term deposits or German federal bonds with staggered maturities and a settlement account. This is feasible, but it requires a decision every few years, and at 88 the ability to make such decisions can no longer be taken for granted. An immediate annuity, by contrast, continues without any action on your part and thus also solves this problem.

bloecke.md:
## Break-even age of the immediate annuity

The obvious break-even calculation presents the policy in too favourable a light. Dividing €100,000 by an annual pension of €3,684 gives 27.1 years; at 92 you would therefore have got back the money paid in. However, this calculation assumes that the money would earn no interest in the alternative. A comparison with an interest-bearing account from which exactly the same amount is withdrawn is more informative.

The assumptions are €100,000 in an account paying 2% interest and an annual withdrawal of €3,684, equal to the guaranteed pension.

- The account sustains this withdrawal for 39.5 years, that is, up to the age of 104.
- With the projected pension of €380 a month (€4,560 a year), it is 29.2 years, that is, up to the age of 94.

The immediate annuity therefore only pays off if you live longer than almost everyone else. That is its purpose. It is insurance against the event that you yourself are one of these exceptions, and not an investment. Like any insurance, it does not pay off in terms of expected value.

Measured by expected value, an immediate annuity is expensive; measured by the worst case, it is cheap. Anyone who buys one pays for the certainty that the pension will still be paid at 97, not for a return.

## Taxes and social security contributions

A private life annuity from taxed capital (layer 3) is only taxed on the **taxable income portion**. This is 18% if the pension starts at 65 or 66 and 17% at 67, and it falls further if the pension starts later, for example to 11% at 75 and 8% at 80 (Section 22 no. 1 sentence 3 letter a double letter bb EStG, Income Tax Act). The rest remains tax-free for life. With a monthly pension of €307 from 65, €663 a year is therefore taxable. At a marginal tax rate of 25%, this results in around €166 of tax, that is, 4.5% of the pension.

It is often overlooked that private pensions in layer 3 are not pension-type income (Versorgungsbezüge) within the meaning of Section 229 SGB V (Social Code Book V, health insurance). For members of the health insurance for pensioners (Krankenversicherung der Rentner), they are therefore free of contributions. If a company pension exceeds €197.75 a month, by contrast, the full health insurance contribution of around 17.5% in 2026 is payable on the part above this allowance, and 3.6% for long-term care insurance from the first euro. The exemption from contributions does not apply to voluntarily insured pensioners, because under Section 240 SGB V their entire economic capacity counts.

bloecke.md: With a withdrawal plan, only the interest portion is taxable, and when fund units are sold, only the gain portion. For equity funds, in turn, only 70% of this is taxable, because a 30% partial exemption applies (Section 20 InvStG, Investment Tax Act). The saver's allowance of €1,000 (Section 20(9) EStG) covers a considerable part at these orders of magnitude. If the personal tax rate in retirement is below 25%, the tax office refunds the difference via the most-favourable assessment (Günstigerprüfung) under Section 32d(6) EStG. The most-favourable assessment must be applied for in the tax return.

## Splitting according to basic needs

The decision is how much capital goes into an immediate annuity and how much stays in the portfolio. A sound split is based on expenses, not on assets. The unavoidable monthly expenses for housing, energy, insurance, food and transport should be covered by income guaranteed for life. For all other expenses, income may fluctuate.

Basic needs amount to €2,000 a month. Since July 2026, the standard pension from 45 earnings points (Entgeltpunkte) has been around €1,913 gross. After deducting 8.75% for health insurance, 3.6% for long-term care insurance (4.2% for childless persons) and around €58 of income tax (single, without church tax, pension starting in 2026), around €1,619 remains.

- The gap in basic needs is €381 a month. Because the taxable income portion of the immediate annuity is also taxed, the annuity must amount to around €397.
- With a guaranteed annuity conversion factor of 30.7, this results in a capital requirement of 397 ÷ 30.7 × 10,000 = around €129,000.
- With assets of €250,000, around €129,000 is therefore annuitised, and €121,000 remains in the portfolio for travel, dental prosthetics, the car, the grandchildren and a care home place that may become necessary.

Here, just over half of the assets would be annuitised. Anyone who pays everything into the policy gives up all flexibility for a degree of security that they only partly need.

## Inflation and the purchasing power of the pension

The greatest weakness of the immediate annuity is less the annuity conversion factor than its nominally fixed amount. A pension of €307 is still €307 even after 25 years. The statutory pension, by contrast, is adjusted, for example by 4.24% on 1 July 2026 to a current pension value (aktueller Rentenwert) of €42.52. The benchmark here is wages and not prices; in the years 2021 to 2023, the adjustment was below the rate of price increases more than once. A private immediate annuity has no such adjustment mechanism. It only rises if surpluses arise, and these depend on the insurer's investment income and not on the consumer price index.

bloecke.md: There are escalating immediate annuities that rise by a fixed percentage every year. In return, they start with a considerably lower pension, and it takes many years to make up the shortfall. The part of the assets that was not annuitised provides more effective protection against inflation. That is why the combination of the two building blocks is more than a compromise. The policy secures basic needs, and the portfolio offsets rising prices.

The annuity conversion factor rises markedly with the age at entry, because the calculated remaining term becomes shorter. When annuitising in tranches, only part of the capital is annuitised at 65, and a further tranche is bought at 75 or 80. Until then, the capital remains invested in the portfolio, and the later pension is bought more cheaply.

In practice, this means annuitising at retirement only as much as basic needs less the statutory pension require. The second decision is deliberately postponed to an age at which you know your own state of health and your actual spending. When comparing offers, the only thing that counts is the guaranteed annuity conversion factor for the same single premium, the same age and the same annuity guarantee period (Rentengarantiezeit).

Two add-ons reduce the loss that arises in the event of early death. With an **annuity guarantee period**, the pension continues to be paid to the surviving dependants after death until the end of the agreed period. A **capital refund** (Kapitalrückgewähr) reimburses the part of the single premium not yet used up. Both lower the annuity conversion factor, the capital refund considerably more than a ten-year guarantee period. The capital refund removes the balancing between early and late deaths on which the entire calculation of the annuity is based. Wealth can be passed on more cheaply through the non-annuitised part of the portfolio than through an add-on in the policy.

bloecke.titel: Payout from the retirement investment account
bloecke.md:
The retirement investment account (Altersvorsorgedepot), subsidised from 2027, offers a choice at payout. At the start of the pension, up to 30% of the balance may be withdrawn as a partial lump sum. The rest is paid out either as a lifelong life annuity or as a withdrawal plan that ends at the age of 85 at the earliest and then pays out the remaining capital. The Retirement Provision Reform Act (Altersvorsorgereformgesetz) of 26 May 2026 no longer requires subsequent annuitisation. Under the previous Riester contract, a withdrawal plan had to switch to annuitisation of part of the capital at 85 at the latest.

This previous Riester rule follows the same reasoning as this lesson. A withdrawal plan covers the probable years of life at low cost, and annuitisation insures against improbably long lives. Anyone who chooses the withdrawal plan for the retirement investment account has to arrange this protection themselves.

mitnehmen: The annuity conversion factor is the only figure with which immediate annuities can be compared; projected pensions include surpluses to which there is no entitlement.
The guarantee lowers the pension, because the technical interest rate and costs turn a fixed-term annuity of €372 into a guaranteed monthly pension of around €307 per €100,000.
Compared with an account paying 2% interest, the guaranteed immediate annuity only pays off from an age of over 100, because it is insurance and not an investment.

The private life annuity is favourable for tax purposes, because only a taxable income portion of 17% to 18% is taxed if the pension starts between 65 and 67 (Section 22 EStG), and compulsorily insured persons pay no health or long-term care insurance contributions on it.
The yardstick for annuitisation is the gap in basic needs, not the assets; the non-annuitised part serves to offset inflation, provides flexibility and forms the inheritance.

begriffe.text: Guaranteed monthly pension per €10,000 of capital. The annuity conversion factor combines the technical interest rate, mortality table and costs of an annuity contract into a single comparable figure.
Pension insurance paid for with a single premium that pays a lifelong pension immediately, without an accumulation phase. The insured risk is that of living longer than your own capital lasts.

Taxable part of a private life annuity from taxed capital. It is 18% if the pension starts at 65, 17% at 67, and falls further if the pension starts later (Section 22 EStG); the rest remains tax-free for life.
The risk of living considerably longer than average life expectancy and using up your own capital in the process. It can only be handed over completely with a lifelong pension.
Agreed period during which the pension continues to be paid to surviving dependants even after the death of the insured person. An annuity guarantee period lowers the annuity conversion factor.
